# `silk/schema/codec`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Two-way conversions between a value and its form on the wire, and checks that refine them.

## When to use
Implement [`Codec`](#Codec) for a conversion that a format cannot do by itself, such as a port number
written as text. Run several steps in order with [`Codecs.chain2`](#Codecs.impl.chain2) to [`Codecs.chain6`](#Codecs.impl.chain6), and
attach a check to a step with [`Codecs.check`](#Codecs.impl.check), so a multi-step conversion is written once and
runs in both directions.

## Details
A `Codec<A, I>` decodes a wire value `I` into a value `A`, and encodes `A` back into `I`.
Decoding can fail with an [`Issue`](./schema-issue.md#Issue); encoding cannot, because a value that exists already passed
its checks. A chain is an ordinary value whose type records each step, such as
`Chain3<Trim, Refine<NumberText<u16>, ...>, PortOf, ...>`, so decoding is direct calls with no
codec object left at runtime.

Decoding runs the steps from the wire form to the value, and encoding runs them the other way.
A check added with `Codecs.check` runs on decode only, on the value its step produced.

## Gotchas
A step of a chain must not be another chain, and the codec inside `Codecs.check` must not be a
chain: the compiler rejects the nested specialization (`SEM0053`). Use one longer chain instead.

## Examples
### Read a port from text
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.schema.codec { Between, Codec, Codecs, NumberText, Trim }
import silk.schema.issue { Issue }
import silk.text.string { String }

effect fn port(text: string) -> u16 ! Issue | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let codec = Codecs.chain2(Trim {}, Codecs.check(NumberText<u16>.make(),
    Between<u16> {low: 1, high: 65535, message: "between 1 and 65535"}))
  return run Codec.decode(&codec, run String.copy(text))
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let parsed = run Effect.result(port(" 8080 ")) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  return match move parsed {
    Result<u16, Issue | OutOfMemoryError>.Success {value} => if value == 8080 { 0 } else { 1 }
    Result<u16, Issue | OutOfMemoryError>.Failure {..} => 2
  }
}
```

Import as `Codec` with `import silk.schema.codec { Codec }`.

## `Codec`

```silk
pub interface Codec<A, I>
```

A two-way conversion between a value `A` and its wire form `I`.

### When to use

Implement it for a conversion step, such as text to a number. Combine steps with
[`Codecs.chain2`](#Codecs.impl.chain2) and [`Codecs.check`](#Codecs.impl.check) rather than writing one large implementation.

### Details

`decode` takes the wire value by value, so owned text moves through a chain without copies.
`encode` borrows the value. A codec type usually has no fields, or holds the static settings of
its step, such as the bounds of a range.

<a id="Codec.decode"></a>

### Operation `decode`

```silk
effect fn decode(self: &Self, input: I) -> A ! Issue | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Converts the wire value `input` into a value.

#### Errors

- `Issue` if `input` does not hold an acceptable value.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the value needs memory that the `Allocator` cannot supply.

<a id="Codec.encode"></a>

### Operation `encode`

```silk
effect fn encode(self: &Self, value: &A) -> I ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Converts `value` back into its wire form.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the wire form needs memory that the `Allocator` cannot supply.

<a id="Check"></a>

## `Check`

```silk
pub interface Check<T>
```

A test that a decoded value must pass, with the message a person sees when it fails.

### When to use

Implement it for a rule a type cannot express, such as a length limit, and attach it to a codec
with [`Codecs.check`](#Codecs.impl.check).

<a id="Check.test"></a>

### Operation `test`

```silk
fn test(self: &Self, value: &T) -> bool
```

Returns whether `value` passes.

<a id="Check.message"></a>

### Operation `message`

```silk
fn message(self: &Self) -> string<'static>
```

Returns what the check expects, as one line for a person, such as `"between 1 and 64"`.

<a id="NumberText"></a>

## `NumberText`

```silk
pub struct NumberText<T>
```

The codec between an integer and its decimal text, such as `"8080"` and `8080`.

### Details

It is implemented for `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`, `usize`, `i8`, `i16`, `i32` and `i64`. Decoding
accepts an optional sign and decimal digits, and fails with `IssueReason.InvalidType` for other
text and `IssueReason.InvalidValue` for a number that does not fit.

<a id="NumberText.kind"></a>

### Field `kind`

```silk
pub kind: [T; 0]
```

Empty. It names the integer type.

<a id="Items"></a>

## `Items`

```silk
pub struct Items<T>
```

The check that a list of `T` has between `min` and `max` elements, both included.

### When to use

Build it with [`Items.between`](#Items.impl.between), such as `Items<String>.between(1, 8, "1 to 8 tags")`.

<a id="Codecs"></a>

## `Codecs`

```silk
pub struct Codecs
```

The owner of the functions that combine codecs. It has no fields and is never constructed.

<a id="Codecs.impl"></a>

## Implementation `Codecs`

```silk
impl Codecs
```

<a id="Codecs.impl.chain2"></a>

### Associated function `chain2`

```silk
pub fn chain2<A, M1, I, S1: Codec<M1, I>, S2: Codec<A, M1>>(step1: S1, step2: S2) -> Chain2<S1, S2, A, M1, I>
```

Returns the codec that runs two steps in order: decoding from `step1` to `step2`, and
encoding the other way.

#### Details

Each step's value must be the next step's wire form. A mismatch is a type error at the call.

<a id="Codecs.impl.check"></a>

### Associated function `check`

```silk
pub fn check<A, I, C: Codec<A, I>, K: Check<A>>(codec: C, check: K) -> Refine<C, K, A, I>
```

Returns the codec that decodes with `codec` and fails if `check` rejects the value.

#### Details

Encoding uses `codec` alone, because a value that exists already passed the check.
